correctness.rationale: The stationary problem reduces exactly to (I+rH)z=-rδ on an n-1 dimensional zero-total-mass subspace. Irreducibility proves invertibility and positive denominator at r>0, detailed balance eliminates the constant term, and the adjugate degree bound proves ≤n-2 positive zeros. The triangle example is independently checked by exact rational stationary elimination. Finite tests support but do not constitute the general proof.

The general discrete-time minimal ratchet, thermally driven six-state motor, continuum QSS flashing diffusion, and pump no-go theorem address different claims or impose different hypotheses. value.rationale: The bound constrains experimentally relevant sign reversals independently of microscopic reversible rates and is attained in the smallest cycle. It differentiates a structural two-environment response ceiling from behavior requiring additional phase states or rate changes, giving a falsifiable model-class diagnostic rather than just a computed small-instance formula.
